skill.name: sprint-retrospective
skill.description: Facilitate structured sprint retrospectives with proven formats, focused discussion prompts, and practical follow-up actions.
skill.summary: Guide agile teams through structured sprint retrospectives and action planning.
skill.author: supercent-io

content.value_statement: Sprint teams need structured reflection to turn issues into practical improvements. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through retrospective formats, action items, and follow-up practices.
actual_capabilities: Produces Start-Stop-Continue, Mad-Sad-Glad, and 4Ls retrospective outlines.
Turns sprint notes into grouped discussion themes.
Creates two or three specific action items with owners.
Adds follow-up checks for the next retrospective.
Frames discussion around safe, process-focused feedback.
limitations: Requires user-provided sprint context, team notes, and metrics.
Does not connect directly to project management tools.
Cannot enforce action item completion after the meeting.
Does not replace skilled human facilitation for sensitive conflicts.

use_cases.title: Prepare an End-of-Sprint Session
use_cases.description: Create a focused retrospective agenda, format, and action item structure for a completed sprint.

use_cases.title: Turn Feedback Into Improvements
use_cases.description: Group team comments into themes and convert them into clear process changes.

use_cases.title: Review a Release Milestone
use_cases.description: Capture lessons from a delivery milestone and identify practical follow-up work.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Retrospective Outline
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with simple sprint details.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Start-Stop-Continue retrospective for Sprint 14. We completed 21 points, missed one story, and found two bugs. Include two action items.

prompt_templates.title: Theme Team Notes
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn these team notes into a Mad-Sad-Glad retrospective. Group repeated themes, remove blame, and create action items with owners.

prompt_templates.title: Facilitate 4Ls Discussion
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a 60-minute 4Ls retrospective for a cross-functional team. Include time boxes, prompts, voting guidance, and follow-up steps.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Improvement Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request after a difficult sprint.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this sprint data and feedback. Identify systemic issues, choose the best retrospective format, and propose a two-sprint improvement plan.

output_examples.input: A scrum master asks for a basic retrospective after a sprint with missed documentation work.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a Start-Stop-Continue agenda with documentation themes, two action items, owners, and a next-retro follow-up check.

output_examples.input: An engineering manager provides notes about deployment issues, delayed reviews, and strong teamwork.
output_examples.output: The skill groups the notes into Mad, Sad, and Glad themes, then proposes a release checklist and review-time reservation.

output_examples.input: A product team lead wants a milestone retrospective after a major release.
output_examples.output: The skill creates a 4Ls structure with prompts for delivery learning, process gaps, and practical improvements for the next release.

best_practices: Provide sprint metrics, incidents, and team feedback before asking for output.
Limit action items to two or three items with clear owners.
Review previous action items before generating a new retrospective.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill to assign personal blame.
Do not create a long action list with no owners.
Do not skip follow-up on earlier improvement commitments.

faq.question: Which retrospective formats does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports Start-Stop-Continue, Mad-Sad-Glad, and 4Ls formats.

faq.question: Can it create action items?
faq.answer: Yes. It creates specific action items with owners and follow-up guidance when context is provided.

faq.question: Does it need sprint metrics?
faq.answer: Metrics are not required, but they improve the quality of the retrospective output.

faq.question: Can it handle sensitive team conflicts?
faq.answer: It can suggest process-focused wording, but a human facilitator should manage serious conflict.

faq.question: Does it integrate with Jira or Linear?
faq.answer: No. It only generates retrospective content from information supplied in the prompt.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
